To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) precise dynamic slicing algorithms are faster than imprecise algorithms for small numbers of slicing requests, (2) precise dynamic slicing can be made faster than imprecisive slicing for larger numbers of requests by using the limited preprocessing technique.
the LP slicing algorithm is fast, practical and precise.

the NP algorithm is the fastest of the three algorithms but is not precise, the LP algorithm computes the same slices as the FP algorithm but is much faster, and the LP algorithm is the fastest practical precise dynamic slicing algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of dynamic slicing algorithms that are precise and fast.
the design and evaluation (both in theory and practice) of dynamic slicing algorithms.
the design and evaluation (using a large set of real-life programs) of a new dynamic slicing algorithm that is precise and practical.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the class of programs we have experimented, the LP algorithm produces precise slices that are smaller than imprecisely computed slices, and is as fast or faster than imprecise algorithms.
the LP algorithm should be used as the precise slicing algorithm of choice.
the LP algorithm provides the best of both worlds: precise slicing and fast execution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for large programs with a small number of slicing request, precise dynamic slices are both small and fast to compute.
for a small number of slicing request, the LP algorithm computes precise dynamic slices faster than the imprecise algorithm.

for a small number of slicing request, the LP algorithm can be used to compute precise slices that are much smaller than the slices computed by imprecise dynamic algorithms, and at the same time the LP algorithm is fast enough to be used for interactive program debugging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of precise dynamic slicing algorithms is not a solved problem and that further work is needed to develop practical algorithms.
the dynamic slice can be a very useful debugging tool.
the relative speed and precision of a slicing algorithm is dependent on the number of slicing requests.
